title: Drain fly treatment
subtitle: Filled in 6 Nov 2026 from Australian government sources, not from Mitch. Items marked in orange are for Mitch to confirm.

sections.heading: When this job comes up
body: Customer has drain flies. Mitch's service is called Drain Fly Treatment. Past invoices read: "Drain fly treatment", "Drain fly treatment, second treatment" and "External fly treatment only including residual treatment to common fly activity areas around the property".

Drain flies (also called moth flies) breed where it is damp and there is a build-up of organic gunk, like bathroom drains, open drains and septic run-off. So the fix is the breeding spot, not just the flies you can see. [Mitch to confirm: from Victorian Government pest control technical note on flies and Shire of Coolgardie fly fact sheet, not from Mitch]
The job process, the never list, PPE and the free service period are in the Every job guide. [Mitch to confirm: does the free service period apply to this job?]

sections.heading: How to tell it is drain fly
rows: Tiny dark grey flies, 2 to 4 mm

Drain (moth) flies. The body is covered in fine hairs, and the wings are moth-like with a hairy fringe. [Mitch to confirm: from Victorian Government pest control technical note on flies, not from Mitch]
Flies around bathrooms, open drains or septic run-off
That is where moth flies are usually found, anywhere it is damp. [Mitch to confirm: from Victorian Government pest control technical note on flies, not from Mitch]
Small brown and yellow or brown and black flies, 2.5 to 4 mm, around fruit and veg

Not drain flies. They are vinegar (fruit) flies. They go for ripe or rotting fruit and veg. [Mitch to confirm: from Victorian Government pest control technical note on flies and Shire of Coolgardie fly fact sheet, not from Mitch]

items.a: Drain flies, also called moth flies. They're tiny, dark grey and hairy, and they look a bit like a little moth. You find them where it's damp, like bathrooms and drains. [Mitch to confirm: from Victorian Government pest control technical note on flies, not from Mitch]

items.q: Why do I keep getting them?
items.a: They breed in the damp build-up in and around drains. New flies keep turning up until the breeding spot is dealt with, so that's what we treat. [Mitch to confirm: from Victorian Government pest control technical note on flies and Shire of Coolgardie fly fact sheet, not from Mitch]

items.q: Are they the same as fruit flies?
items.a: No. Fruit flies go for ripe or rotting fruit and veg. Drain flies come from damp build-up in drains. [Mitch to confirm: from Victorian Government pest control technical note on flies and Shire of Coolgardie fly fact sheet, not from Mitch]

Only in big numbers is there any concern, and that's an allergic reaction in some people if they breathe them in. Sorting out the breeding spot is the fix. [Mitch to confirm: from Victorian Government pest control technical note on flies, not from Mitch. Check you are happy with this wording]

items.q: How do I stop them coming back?
items.a: Keep the damp spots clean so gunk doesn't build up, keep bins closed and dry, and use screens on windows and doors where you can. [Mitch to confirm: from Victorian Government pest control technical note on flies and Shire of Coolgardie fly fact sheet, not from Mitch]

items.q: Is it safe for the kids and pets?
items.a: Keep kids and pets out of the area while we treat. Follow the product label for when it's safe to come back in. We normally say 1 to 2 hours once it's dry. [Mitch to confirm: from Better Health Channel (Victorian Government) and the Every job guide, not from Mitch]
